document.title: MoHFW and WHO organize National Influenza Chintan Shivir for seasonal preparedness
document.text: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, in collaboration with the World Health Organization, inaugurated a two-day Influenza Chintan Shivir in New Delhi to review seasonal influenza preparedness ahead of peak winter transmission. Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda highlighted the role of the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) in monitoring Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) and Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) across sentinel sites. Virological surveillance confirmed that circulating strains remain predominantly seasonal influenza A(H3N2) and B(Victoria), with low community transmission and no emerging antigenic drift.

document.title: High-level review indicates seasonal respiratory infections remain within baseline levels
document.text: Union Health Secretary chaired a review meeting with the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) and ICMR experts to assess winter respiratory illness trends. Data collected from 28 state surveillance units indicated that total ILI hospital presentations are consistent with five-year seasonal averages. No localized clustering or unexpected mortality was observed. States were advised to ensure standard infection control protocols and maintain adequate stockpiles of oseltamivir and viral transport media.

document.title: Health Minister issues preventive advisory to States for dengue and malaria management
document.text: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda addressed an advisory to Chief Ministers emphasizing intensified community-led source reduction to preempt post-monsoon vector proliferation. Over 5,520 dengue and 2,530 chikungunya IgM diagnostic test kits have been supplied to 869 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals nationwide. The advisory instructed municipal bodies to monitor Breteau indices and execute targeted indoor space sprays in urban clusters where intermittent rains had caused water stagnation.

document.title: India reaffirms commitment to malaria elimination on World Malaria Day 2025
document.text: On World Malaria Day 2025, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare released national surveillance statistics indicating an 85% decline in total malaria cases and a 79% reduction in malaria deaths compared to 2015 baselines. Under the National Framework for Malaria Elimination (NFME) 2016-2030, over 124 districts have sustained zero indigenous malaria cases for three consecutive years and are preparing for sub-national elimination certification.
